_what: Narration outline for flagship long-form #1 'House Bugs Ranked' (TASKS: FLAGSHIP LONG-FORM #1, FLAGSHIP NEEDS A STORY, LONG-FORM ANIMATION FIXES; MEATBALL_ORDERS QUALITY FIRST). 2 AM mystery: six suspects, one per room; centipede twist and comment prompt near 3:30; bed bug climax in Meatball's bed. Every factual line carries src = fact IDs (P5 silverfish QA, P4/P4Q centipede, DM/HS/CR/BB packs; see sources). vis = what the picture must show. card = on-screen card text. Lines without rate/pitch use the top-level voice settings. Readable script with timestamps: side-hustles/channels/scripts/longform-house-bugs-ranked.md.
titles: House Bugs Ranked by Meatball, From Harmless to Get Out
Six House Bugs, Ranked by How Worried Meatball Is
House Bugs Ranked: What Bit Me at 2 AM?

lines.say: It's 2 AM, and something in this house bit me.
lines.vis: FRAME 0: flashlight snaps on, a house centipede FILLS the frame on the hallway wall (tease). Hard cut at 0:02 to Meatball BIG (half the frame), rubbing his arm, lamp-pool light.

lines.say: Tonight, I find out exactly what it was.
lines.vis: Camera move by 0:04: fast push-in on Meatball's eyes narrowing. Flashlight click SFX.

lines.say: Six suspects live in this house with me.
lines.vis: Cut: the tier board slams in (HARMLESS / ANNOYING / GROSS / GET OUT) with 6 dark silhouettes lined up under it.

lines.say: I'm ranking every one, from harmless to get out.
lines.vis: Whip-pan along the silhouettes; each one twitches as the camera passes.

lines.say: One of them might be in your house right now.
lines.vis: Cut: the camera turns to face the viewer, flashlight beam into the lens.

lines.say: And number one is not the one you think.
lines.vis: Snap back to the centipede on the wall; it bolts out of frame. Sound hit. Meatball grabs the flashlight and heads for the bathroom (camera tracks low).

lines.say: Suspect one is sitting in my bathtub.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 1 OF 6' + sound hit. Flashlight sweeps the dry tub; a silverfish in the beam.

lines.say: Silverfish: its fossils date to 400 million years ago.
lines.vis: BUG CAM (interrupt): low fish-eye shot from the tub floor, silverfish huge. BUG ID card row 1 slides in.
lines.card: BUG ID: SILVERFISH · FOSSILS: 400 MILLION YEARS AGO

lines.say: That's about twice as long ago as the dinosaurs.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball stacks a tiny dinosaur toy on a timeline rope, then walks twice as far to put the silverfish down.

lines.say: They move rapidly, including sideways, and their flat bodies let them hide in narrow crevices.
lines.vis: Cut: silverfish zips sideways along the tub rim (Meatball's head whips left-right), then camera follows it flat into the grout line.
lines.card: ID ROW 2: FAST, EVEN SIDEWAYS · ID ROW 3: FLAT, HIDES IN CREVICES

lines.say: So, suspect one: did you bite me?
lines.vis: Interrogation: desk lamp swings over the tub, Meatball leans in close.

lines.say: Its very weak jaws scrape the surface of paper instead of biting it.
lines.vis: Cut: close on a book page being scraped thin; slow push-in for the long line.

lines.say: That's about paper, not people, so it stays on my list.
lines.vis: CASE BOARD overlay (graphic, not a room): Meatball pins a SILVERFISH photo to a corkboard.

lines.say: Also, silverfish do not transmit disease.
lines.vis: Quick cut: a green check stamp on the corkboard photo.

lines.say: Why is it here? They can invade new homes from wild areas nearby.
lines.vis: Card WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?, then cut to the bathroom window: a little silverfish parade crossing the sill from a dry field outside.

lines.say: Especially as those areas dry out in summer.
lines.vis: Act it out: a sun dial over the field spins to SUMMER; the grass browns.

lines.say: If they fall in a bathtub or sink, they can't climb up the slippery sides.
lines.vis: Back in the tub: the silverfish slides back down the wall twice. Camera tilts up the tub wall.

lines.say: They can't crawl up through the drain, either.
lines.vis: Cut: Meatball peers into the drain with the flashlight. Nothing there.

lines.say: What should I do? Look for dustlike scales around damaged books.
lines.vis: Card. Meatball holds a chewed book under the flashlight; glitter-like scales on the shelf.

lines.say: All that history, and it loses to a bathtub.
lines.vis: Meatball salutes the silverfish in the tub; it salutes back with a feeler.

lines.say: It damages paper, books and wallpaper, so: annoying.
lines.vis: Whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic (no room behind it); the silverfish card drops into ANNOYING. Sound hit.

lines.say: Then I spot a trail of dust leading to the couch.
lines.vis: Flashlight follows a dust trail down the stairs to the living-room couch.

lines.say: Suspect two lives in my couch, and I can't even see it.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 2 OF 6' + sound hit. Meatball squints at a couch cushion.

lines.say: Dust mites: adults are about half a millimeter long.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball drags in a huge toy microscope and a ruler to the cushion; a counter zooms 1x...10x...100x into a single mite.
lines.card: BUG ID: DUST MITE · ABOUT 0.5 MM

lines.say: Their primary food is skin flakes in house dust.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball scratches his ear; flakes float down into the cushion like snow; mites cheer.
lines.card: ID ROW 2: EATS SHED SKIN FLAKES

lines.say: They tend to be most numerous in beds, overstuffed sofas and chairs.
lines.vis: Camera pulls back across the living room: bed, sofa, armchair each glow briefly.
lines.card: ID ROW 3: MOST IN BEDS, SOFAS, CHAIRS

lines.say: So, did a dust mite bite me?
lines.vis: Interrogation lamp over the cushion.

lines.say: House dust mites are not capable of biting or stinging humans.
lines.vis: Cut: the mite under the microscope shrugs; a red CLEARED stamp hits its card on the corkboard.

lines.say: Why is it here? Every home has dust mites.
lines.vis: Card. Quick montage: three different houses, each with a microscope-view mite waving.
lines.card: WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?
lines.src: DM6 (EPA wording; do not blend with ALA)

lines.say: The trouble, if you're allergic, is allergens in the mites, their cast skins and droppings.
lines.vis: Act it out: a tiny shed skin and a speck labelled POOP float up past Meatball's nose.

lines.say: What should I do? Wash bedding in hot water once a week, and dry it completely.
lines.vis: Card. Cut to a washing machine; the dial clicks to AT LEAST 130°F.
lines.card: WHAT SHOULD YOU DO? · HOT WASH, ONCE A WEEK

lines.say: Meatball's laundry pile just got a lot scarier.
lines.vis: Cut: hygrometer needle drops under 50.

lines.say: I have been napping on a skin-flake buffet.
lines.vis: Meatball stares at the couch, horrified; slow zoom.

lines.say: Dust mites go on the board: annoying, if you're allergic.
lines.vis: Whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic; dust-mite card drops into ANNOYING.

lines.say: But something spun a web across the garage window.
lines.vis: Flashlight beam lands on a web glinting in the garage door window.

lines.say: Suspect three usually hangs belly-up in an irregular web.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 3 OF 6' + sound hit. Garage, cellar spider upside down in a tangled corner web; then SPIDER CAM (interrupt): spider's-eye view of Meatball's giant face.
lines.card: SUSPECT 3 OF 6 · BUG ID: HOUSE SPIDER · ROW 1: USUALLY HANGS BELLY-UP

lines.say: But the jaws of most spiders are too small to bite humans.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball holds a tiny cartoon spider jaw next to his giant paw; the jaw can't reach around.
lines.card: ID ROW 2: MOST JAWS TOO SMALL TO BITE HUMANS

lines.say: So, did a spider bite me last night?
lines.vis: Interrogation lamp swings up to the corner web.

lines.say: Generally, a spider only tries to bite if squeezed, lain on, or similarly provoked.
lines.vis: Three quick cuts: a hand squeezing (stops short), a pillow lowering (stops short), a finger poking (stops short).

lines.say: Some spiders might bite when trapped in clothing or bedding.
lines.vis: Cut: Meatball's own blanket; he slowly lifts it, eyes huge.

lines.say: The effect is usually no more severe than itching or the reaction to a bee sting.
lines.vis: Push-in on Meatball scratching, then shrugging; spider photo pinned to the corkboard with a question mark.

lines.say: Why here? It's commonly found in garages and other dark, quiet, protected spots.
lines.vis: Card. Slow pan across the dark garage shelves; the spider's web in a quiet corner.
lines.card: WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?

lines.say: This longbodied cellar spider is not known to be in any way harmful.
lines.vis: Slow tilt down the spider's long legs; label CELLAR SPIDER.
lines.card: ID ROW 3: CELLAR SPIDER · NOT KNOWN TO BE HARMFUL

lines.say: Only a few spiders, like black widows and brown recluses, have venom very toxic to humans.
lines.vis: Card. Two WANTED posters slam onto the garage wall (black widow, brown recluse), drawn clearly.

lines.say: Not sure what it is? Save it and ask your county extension office.
lines.vis: Cut: a blurry phone photo; a big red NO; then a sharp photo going to an EXPERT ID box.
lines.card: ASK YOUR COUNTY EXTENSION OFFICE · SEVERE BITE: CALL A DOCTOR

lines.say: If a bite causes an unusual or severe reaction, call a doctor.
lines.vis: Meatball holds up a phone, dials. Card stays.

lines.say: Most house spiders go on the board: annoying, mostly the webs.
lines.vis: Meatball peels web off his face, then whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic; spider card drops into ANNOYING.

lines.say: Then something with way too many legs runs for the basement.
lines.vis: Flashlight catches a flicker of many legs vanishing down the basement stairs.

lines.say: Suspect four: basement security cam, 2:14 AM.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 4 OF 6' + sound hit. SECURITY CAM (interrupt): grainy timestamped view, a house centipede streaks across the floor.

lines.say: House centipede: clocked at about sixteen inches a second.
lines.vis: Cut to full colour. Act it out: a speed counter ticks up to ~16 IN/SEC as it runs past a ruler on the floor.
lines.card: BUG ID: HOUSE CENTIPEDE · ABOUT 16 IN/SEC

lines.say: It can run up your walls to hunt.
lines.vis: Cut: centipede runs up the basement wall (walls only, not the ceiling).
lines.card: ID ROW 2: RUNS UP WALLS TO HUNT

lines.say: Unlike most centipedes, it has well-developed, faceted eyes.
lines.vis: Extreme close-up on its faceted eyes; Meatball's reflection in them.

lines.say: Fast, leggy, and it hunts: that's my biter!
lines.vis: Meatball grabs a giant GET OUT stamp, wind-up, freeze-frame on the stamp mid-air.

lines.say: Will it bite you? Here's the twist.
lines.vis: Record-scratch. Card spins in.

lines.say: Which one is in YOUR house? Comment it.
lines.vis: BIG COMMENT CARD with the six silhouettes while the GET OUT stamp hangs frozen mid-air (cliffhanger); Meatball points at the viewer. Sound hit.
lines.card: WHICH ONE IS IN YOUR HOUSE? COMMENT IT

lines.say: Bites to humans are uncommon, unless it's handled or accidentally pressed against skin.
lines.vis: Slow push-in on the centipede sitting calmly; Meatball's stamp lowers.

lines.say: Its fangs are so small that piercing human skin is difficult.
lines.vis: Act it out: tiny fangs vs a giant skin wall; they barely tap it.

lines.say: I never touched it, so it's probably not my biter.
lines.vis: Meatball drops the GET OUT stamp; the centipede's card slides DOWN past GROSS.

lines.say: Why is it in my house? It feeds on bugs in the home.
lines.vis: Card. Cut: centipede facing a lineup of tiny bugs.
lines.card: WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?

lines.say: That includes cockroaches and, yes, silverfish.
lines.vis: Quick flash-back cut: the silverfish from the tub, looking nervous.

lines.say: It catches them by half pouncing, half lassoing.
lines.vis: Act it out: centipede pounces, legs loop around a cardboard bug like a lasso.

lines.say: What should you do? Don't grab it.
lines.vis: Card. Meatball's paw reaches, then yanks back.

lines.say: Most house centipede infestations can be counted in single digits.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball counts on his paw: 1, 2, 3... a counter stops in single digits.

lines.say: I almost arrested the one that eats roaches.
lines.vis: Meatball sheepishly hands the centipede back its photo.

lines.say: House centipede drops to annoying: creepy, but not my case.
lines.vis: Whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic; centipede card lands in ANNOYING.

lines.say: It eats roaches, so I'm checking the kitchen.
lines.vis: Flashlight swings up the basement stairs toward the kitchen door.

lines.say: Suspect five scatters the second I flip the kitchen light.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 5 OF 6' + sound hit. Light flicks on; roaches scatter from the counter.

lines.say: German cockroach: light brown, about half an inch, two dark stripes.
lines.vis: BUG CAM (interrupt): eye-level behind the toaster, one roach freezes. BUG ID card.
lines.card: BUG ID: GERMAN COCKROACH · ABOUT 1/2 INCH

lines.say: Adult German cockroaches can hide in a crack 1/16 inch wide.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball slides a credit-card-thin gap gauge into a counter crack; the roach slips in.
lines.card: ID ROW 2: ADULTS CAN HIDE IN A 1/16-INCH CRACK

lines.say: Each egg case contains about 30 young.
lines.vis: Act it out: tiny roaches pour from an egg case into a jar; a counter ticks to about 30.
lines.card: ID ROW 3: ABOUT 30 YOUNG PER EGG CASE

lines.say: So, did a roach bite me?
lines.vis: Interrogation lamp over the sink.

lines.say: In extremely heavy infestations, German cockroaches have been reported to bite humans.
lines.vis: Slow push-in on a crowded drawing of a filthy pantry, labelled EXTREMELY HEAVY.

lines.say: I saw one roach, which is not extremely heavy.
lines.vis: Smash cut back to Meatball's tidy kitchen with ONE roach.

lines.say: Their droppings or body parts can trigger asthma.
lines.vis: Cut: an inhaler on the counter; a speck labelled DROPPINGS drifts by.

lines.say: Why is it here? They're often brought in with infested grocery bags.
lines.vis: Card. Cut: a grocery bag set on the counter; a roach climbs out of a carton.
lines.card: WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?

lines.say: Even clean homes can become infested.
lines.vis: Cut: a sparkling kitchen, then one roach strolls through.

lines.say: What should you do? Pesticides alone will not solve cockroach problems.
lines.vis: Card. Meatball drops a spray can; it rolls away.

lines.say: Good sanitation and exclusion are important.
lines.vis: Two quick cuts: Meatball wipes the counter; caulks a crack by the sink.

lines.say: If using insecticides, baits provide better control than sprays.
lines.vis: Cut: a bait station placed near the crack vs a spray can with a big X.

lines.say: Avoid foggers, bombs, or aerosol sprays; they can be hazardous.
lines.vis: Cut: a bug bomb with a red NO stamp (never shown going off).

lines.say: Always read and follow the label.
lines.vis: Close on a label with READ ME highlighted.

lines.say: About thirty babies per egg case? I need a shower.
lines.vis: Meatball shudders head to tail.

lines.say: The cockroach goes on the board: gross.
lines.vis: Whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic; roach card drops into GROSS with a splat SFX.

lines.say: But roaches feed on filth, and my biter feeds solely on blood.
lines.vis: Close on Meatball's arm, the bite mark glows.

lines.say: There's one room I haven't searched: mine.
lines.vis: Kitchen doorway: Meatball's shadow stretches long toward the stairs; creak SFX, slow push-in.

lines.say: Suspect six: last room, my own bed.
lines.vis: RE-HOOK CARD 'SUSPECT 6 OF 6' + heartbeat SFX. Bedroom, lamp pool on the bed.

lines.say: I lift the sheet, check the mattress seam, and...
lines.vis: Slow push-in, flashlight along the mattress seam (camera move, no hold over 5 s).

lines.say: Bed bug! Bed bug! There's a bed bug in my bed!
lines.vis: FREAK-OUT (interrupt): Meatball launches straight up, clings to the ceiling fan, fan spins him round. Fast cuts.

lines.say: Get out, get out, get out!
lines.vis: He drops onto the dresser, then hides behind the curtain, one eye peeking.

lines.say: Adult bed bugs are about 3/16 of an inch, reddish-brown, oval and flat.
lines.vis: Close on the bed bug next to an apple seed for colour only (no size claim from the seed).
lines.card: BUG ID: BED BUG · ABOUT 3/16 INCH

lines.say: They can fit into crevices no wider than a toothpick.
lines.vis: Act it out: a toothpick laid along the headboard crack; the bug slides in beside it.
lines.card: ID ROW 2: FITS A TOOTHPICK-WIDE CRACK

lines.say: They can hide in mattress seams, box springs, bed frames and headboards.
lines.vis: Four quick cuts: seam, box spring, frame, headboard, each with a hidden bug.
lines.card: ID ROW 3: SEAMS · BOX SPRINGS · FRAMES

lines.say: Will it bite you? Yes, and here's how.
lines.vis: Card. Meatball nods slowly, eyes wide.

lines.say: Bed bugs bite people and animals at night while they sleep.
lines.vis: Cut: a sleeping-Meatball flashback, a bug crawling toward his arm (no bite shown).

lines.say: The bite is painless, so people seldom realize they're being bitten.
lines.vis: Flashback Meatball keeps snoring peacefully.

lines.say: Bite marks may take as long as 14 days to develop in some people.
lines.vis: Act it out: calendar pages flip; a counter ticks up to 14 days; the mark appears.

lines.say: Bites can cause itching and loss of sleep. Serious allergic reactions are rare.
lines.vis: Meatball scratching, then wide awake at 3 AM (two quick cuts).

lines.say: Bed bugs are not known to spread diseases to people.
lines.vis: Small relief beat: Meatball exhales.

lines.say: Case closed: I found my biter.
lines.vis: CASE CLOSED stamp slams onto the bed-bug photo on the corkboard. Sound hit.

lines.say: Why is it here? Bed bugs hitchhike in on luggage, clothing and furniture.
lines.vis: Card. Cut: a suitcase opens on the bed; a bug rides out on a sock.
lines.card: WHY IS IT IN MY HOUSE?

lines.say: What should you do? Put bedding and clothes in the dryer on high heat for 30 minutes.
lines.vis: Card. Cut: dryer dial on HIGH, timer 30 MIN.
lines.card: WHAT SHOULD YOU DO? · DRYER, HIGH HEAT, 30 MIN

lines.say: Just washing will generally not kill bed bugs.
lines.vis: Cut: a bug surfing happily in a washing machine.

lines.say: Don't raise your home's temperature with a thermostat, propane space heater or fireplace.
lines.vis: Card. Thermostat, space heater and fireplace each get a big red X (none shown running hot).
lines.card: DON'T HEAT YOUR HOME TO KILL BED BUGS

lines.say: That does not work, and it is dangerous.
lines.vis: Hold on the three X's; camera push-in.

lines.say: Never use a pesticide indoors that's meant for outdoor use.
lines.vis: Cut: an outdoor spray can stopped at the front door by a NO sign.

lines.say: Removal from a home can be expensive and inconvenient.
lines.vis: Act it out: Meatball's piggy bank empties coin by coin.

lines.say: If needed, hire a pest management professional.
lines.vis: Cut: a pro in a uniform knocks; Meatball opens the door, relieved.

lines.say: Professionals have more intensive, proven methods that can even treat whole houses with heat.
lines.vis: Cut: the pro rolls in a big professional heat unit (drawn, generic, no brand).

lines.say: I'm sleeping on the roof tonight.
lines.vis: Meatball on the roof in a sleeping bag, clutching a teddy.

lines.say: Bed bug goes on the board: get out, number one.
lines.vis: Whoosh to the full-screen TIER BOARD graphic; the bed bug card slams into GET OUT with the biggest sound hit of the video.

lines.say: Case closed, so here's the final board.
lines.vis: Roof at dawn, Meatball in his sleeping bag; the full tier board floats in the sky, camera trucks along it.

lines.say: Silverfish, dust mites, spiders and the centipede: annoying.
lines.vis: Each card pulses as named.

lines.say: The cockroach is gross, and the bed bug is get out.
lines.vis: GROSS and GET OUT pulse; the bed-bug card shakes.

lines.say: Harmless has one spot left, and it's mine.
lines.vis: Meatball climbs into the empty HARMLESS slot and curls up, tail wag.

lines.say: Next Wednesday, I crack a brand-new case.
lines.vis: Cut: a new case file stamped CASE #2 slides under the door; a mystery silhouette on it.

lines.say: You pick the suspect: comment the bug I should rank next.
lines.vis: Meatball points at the viewer; comment-bubble icon.
lines.card: WHICH BUG SHOULD I RANK NEXT?

lines.say: Subscribe, and regularly check your mattress seams for bed bugs.
lines.vis: Meatball holds the flashlight to his own mattress seam, side-eye to camera.
END SCREEN, 20 s, nothing important in the corners: House Centipede playlist + House Guests playlist (never a Short), subscribe button. Music only.

_factcheck: Sonnet check 11/17 night: research/facts/house-bugs-ranked-check.md; all spoken and card FIXes applied; Mayo 130F/50% lines replaced (403, unverified) with EPA weekly hot wash + a joke.
fact_files: side-hustles/channels/qa/centipede-p4-1117.md (P4Q-*: the MSU and UKY lines quoted in the 8:10 AM addendum table)
unsourced_cut: "Never bite" / "can't bite you" / "harmless to people" for any bug
Centipede "turns out harmless to people" (TASKS twist wording)
Centipede: 15 pairs of legs, hides in basements/cellars/bathrooms, "dry out the damp", "harmless to pets and the house", "a bite like a bee sting"
Silverfish: dry the air, airtight boxes, toss cardboard
"You've found every one of these in your house" (TASKS cold-open line)
"The next one is in your bed right now" (TASKS re-hook example)
Bed bugs: "EPA: hard to get rid of" as an EPA phrase
House spiders: "why it is in my house" for spiders in general
